constitution-2016.title: Constitution of Zambia (Amendment) Act, No. 2 of 2016
constitution-2016.note: Articles 45-47 (electoral systems), 56 (general elections on the second Thursday of August every five years), 57 (by-elections within ninety days), 58-59 (constituencies, wards, and delimitation), 68 (156 directly elected members of the National Assembly), 101 (election of the President by more than half of the valid votes), 153-154 (councillors, and mayors and council chairpersons elected directly), and 169 (House of Chiefs). Assented to on 5 January 2016; published by the Commission on its legal framework page.

constitution-2025.title: Speech by the Chairperson of the Electoral Commission of Zambia at the first quarter stakeholder meeting, 2026
constitution-2025.note: States that the Constitution of Zambia (Amendment) Act No. 13 of 2025 raised the constituency-based seats from 156 to 226 and introduced a Mixed Member Proportional Representation system for elections to the National Assembly and the councils under Article 47.

delimitation-2026.title: Speech by the Chairperson of the Electoral Commission of Zambia during the announcement of the 70 new constituencies, 16 April 2026
delimitation-2026.note: Gives the history of the constituency count: 75 at independence, 105 from 1968, 125 from 1973, 150 from 1991, 156 from 2016, and 226 from 2026.

epa-2016.title: Electoral Process Act, No. 35 of 2016
epa-2016.note: Conduct of presidential, parliamentary, mayoral, council chairperson, and councillor elections and by-elections, nominations, counting and announcement of results.

epa-bill-2026.title: The Electoral Process (Amendment) Bill, 2026
epa-bill-2026.note: New Part IVA (sections 36A-36F): election of Members of Parliament and councillors under the proportional representation electoral system, with party lists of women, youths, and persons with disabilities.

referendum-act.title: Referendum (Amendment) Act, No. 5 of 2015
referendum-act.note: Amends the Referendum Act (Cap. 14) for the referendum held with the 2016 general election.

ecz-mandate.note: The Commission is established under Article 229 of the Constitution and came into existence as the electoral management body in 1996.

classes.name: Presidential election
classes.locator: Constitution of Zambia (Amendment) Act No. 2 of 2016, arts. 47(1) and 101
classes.finest_note: Constituency in the Commission's public notices; polling-station results are announced but not published as files
classes.note: Elected directly since 1968 (Kenneth Kaunda was first chosen through the January 1964 election to the Legislative Assembly). By plurality until 2016; since the 2016 amendment a candidate needs more than half of the valid votes, with a second round between the top two otherwise. Since 2016 each candidate names a running mate who becomes Vice-President, on the same ballot. A vacancy was filled by presidential by-elections in 2008 and 2015; since 2016 the Vice-President succeeds.

cadence.runoff_rule: second round between the two leading candidates within 37 days when no candidate wins more than half of the valid votes
cadence.vacancy_rule: the Vice-President becomes President for the rest of the term

classes.name: Election of Members of Parliament under the proportional representation electoral system
classes.name_en: National Assembly, party-list members (women, youths, persons with disabilities)
classes.locator: Constitution of Zambia (Amendment) Act No. 13 of 2025, art. 47, as described by the Commission
classes.note: Mixed member proportional representation introduced by Act No. 13 of 2025. Each party contesting the presidency submits lists of twenty women, fifteen youths, and five persons with disabilities (Electoral Process (Amendment) Bill 2026, s. 36C); seats are distributed in proportion to party votes. The number of seats and how the Commission publishes the allocation are not yet confirmed from an official text.

classes.name: Local government elections (ward councillors)
classes.finest_note: Ward in the Commission's public notices of 2011, 2016, and 2021
classes.note: One councillor per ward by first past the post. Held on the same day as the presidential and parliamentary elections since 2001 (tripartite elections); before that in separate local government elections (1992 and 1998 under the Local Government Act 1991). Each council also seats up to three chiefs elected by the district's chiefs (class council_chiefs), and since 2026 list councillors (class council_pr).

classes.name: Election of mayors and council chairpersons by the councillors
classes.name_en: Mayors and council chairpersons chosen by councils (before 2016)
classes.locator: art. 154(2), which made the election direct
classes.disposition_reason: Each council elected its mayor or chairperson from among the councillors at a council meeting; the Commission neither ran nor published these votes.

classes.name: Election of chiefs to councils by the chiefs in the district
classes.disposition_reason: Up to three chiefs per council are chosen by the district's chiefs, not by registered voters, and no results are published.

classes.name: Election of members of the House of Chiefs
classes.disposition_reason: Five chiefs from each province are chosen among the chiefs themselves, not by registered voters; the house advises and does not legislate, and no results are published.

classes.name: Election of the Speaker and Deputy Speakers of the National Assembly
classes.disposition_reason: An internal vote of the National Assembly at its first sitting, recorded in its own proceedings rather than run or published as an election.

classes.name: Party adoption of candidates
classes.locator: s. 2, definition of the adoption certificate signed by a party's secretary-general
classes.disposition_reason: Parties adopt their candidates under their own constitutions and file an adoption certificate; the state neither runs nor publishes any nominating vote.
